beats.subline: Friday, October 16, 2026 close — stocks fell for a second straight day as chipmakers and AI-linked tech names led declines, capping the worst week for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq since June.
beats.body: Micron fell 5.6% and Intel lost 5.8% as investors grew more worried about how long the AI infrastructure spending boom can last, dragging the Nasdaq to its steepest weekly loss since June; the S&P 500 also posted a weekly decline while the Dow still eked out a small weekly gain.

beats.headline: Trump orders military to stay ready for larger Iran strikes after the midterms as US and Iran both claim control of Hormuz
beats.body: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper said the US and regional partners, not Iran, control the Strait of Hormuz and that roughly 400 ships carrying 100 million barrels of oil transited it in the past week despite rising attacks he blamed on IRGC 'desperation'; Iran's acting defense minister countered that Iranian missiles, not US bombs, will decide the war's outcome, as Trump reportedly told the military to stay ready for larger action after the November 3 midterms.

beats.headline: CENTCOM says its Hormuz blockade has cost Iran $25 billion as a tanker is hit by rocket fire off Saudi Arabia
beats.body: Adm. Brad Cooper said the naval blockade of Iranian ports remains 'ironclad,' has cost Tehran about $25 billion in oil export income and led to the seizure of $350 million in Iranian cryptocurrency financing, while US forces have cleared mines from the strait's main shipping lanes; UKMTO logged at least 12 ship attacks in the week ending October 16, including a tanker struck Saturday by a rocket-propelled grenade from a small boat northeast of Jubail, Saudi Arabia.

beats.headline: Hegseth seeks $50 billion to scale autonomous weapons into the millions
beats.body: Speaking at the AUSA conference, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon is seeking roughly $50 billion in one-time reconciliation funding to mass-produce autonomous and robotic systems, saying the department will field 'hundreds of thousands of one-way attack systems this year' and move 'into the millions in years to come'; the request is separate from the FY2027 budget's $53.6 billion Drone Dominance initiative, which includes $16.9 billion for unmanned-system procurement.

beats.headline: Anthropic quietly pitches Capitol Hill its own frontier AI safety bill
beats.body: Politico reported that Anthropic representatives privately shared a confidential draft bill with lawmakers that would let the Commerce Department seek a court order blocking a model's release only where it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damages or of killing or seriously injuring 50-plus people, covering risks like bioweapons, a model evading its developer's controls, or major cyberattacks; an Anthropic spokesperson said the draft reflects proposals from the company's Advanced AI Framework that it has pitched to federal and state lawmakers since June.

beats.headline: Bears list Caleb Williams as questionable for Falcons after a full week of practice
beats.body: The Chicago Sun-Times reported the Bears listed quarterback Caleb Williams as questionable for Sunday's game at Atlanta after he completed a full week of practice coming back from the hamstring strain that has sidelined him since Week 2; running back Kyle Monangai, out with turf toe, was ruled out for the game, and defensive end Montez Sweat remains in the second week of a two-game suspension for a drug policy violation, eligible to return October 23.
